column1: # policy/access/access-verbs.tsv — THE PINNED ACCESS TABLE (the operator's verb
# ALLOW table — THE VOCABULARY DIMENSION).
# THE AUTHOR IS THE OPERATOR (host/deployment), the third host-side author
# beside policy/ops (the operator's PATH rules) and policy/calls (the claim
# judgment).  What makes this table distinct, so it is not a second copy of
# either: policy/ops judges a PATH CLASS (D1/D3) or a RUNTIME STATE (D2), and
# policy/calls judges whether a call is JUSTIFIED.  This table judges the
# VOCABULARY — which verbs may be called AT ALL — over BOTH closed name lists
# at once: the 13 pinned catalog verbs (the guest's fx-verbs vocabulary) UNION
# the host-tool registry (host_time, host_cat — what the HOST executes on the
# allowed path of a judged call).  One grammar, one pin, one author, because a
# table that covered only ONE of the two vocabularies would leave the other
# silently unclassified.
# THIS FILE IS HOST-GLOBAL, NOT PER-GENERATION, and the reason is ROLLBACK:
# the store keeps old generations, and a grant stored per-generation means
# rolling back to an older generation ROLLS THE GRANT BACK — including back to
# a WIDER grant a later release deliberately removed.  A bound a rollback can
# widen is not a bound.  (Second reason, the tree decided it once already for
# ops: a per-generation artifact is what the per-boot record cannot see.  See
# policy/ops/ops-sandbox.tsv's header — do not re-open that decision.)
# SILENCE IS NOT AN ALLOW, AND THERE IS NO THIRD STATE: a name in either
# vocabulary with NO row here is an UNCLASSIFIED VERB, and the loader REFUSES
# TO START on it (a named exit-1, before the slave path is published) rather
# than letting it through.  That is THE TOTALITY CHECK, and both failure
# directions are why it exists: a per-name ALLOW list silently allows every
# FUTURE verb (the day a 14th verb lands in the catalog, the vocabulary widens
# with no gate firing), and a per-name DENY list silently denies a typo while
# allowing everything else.  A name in NEITHER vocabulary (a misspelling) is
# also refused, and so is a duplicate row.
# EXACT NAMES ONLY — no globs, no regex.  The flag column is exactly `allow`
# or `deny`; a row is `verb<TAB>allow|deny` and nothing more.
# SLICE S1 STATUS — READ THIS BEFORE READING THE ROWS.
# THIS TABLE IS NOT CONSULTED YET.  S1 delivers the INERT writer: the table
# exists, is pinned, is loaded and totality-checked at startup, and is
# INSPECTABLE at rest (`build/fx-hostgate --access-dir policy/access
# --print-access`).  NOTHING is judged by it: call_judge does not read it, so
# EVERY call is judged exactly as before this file existed.  A table that is
# loaded and validated but never consulted is INDISTINGUISHABLE — to a reader —
# from one that is enforced, which is why the startup line says so out loud and
# why this paragraph exists.  The enforcement seat is the NEXT slice; until it
# lands, do not describe this file as a bound.
# WHY EVERY ROW BELOW SAYS `allow`: this table classifies the CURRENT
# vocabulary as it actually is — every catalog verb is callable by the guest
# today, and both host tools are in the registry.  The rows are a
# CLASSIFICATION, not yet a narrowing; the day a verb is set to `deny` is a
# release that says so.  Starting from the true state means arming the seat
# (the next slice) changes no existing behaviour, so any later change in reach
# is visibly the table's doing rather than the arming's.
# Columns (TAB-separated; '#' starts a comment):
#   verb        an EXACT name from ONE of the two closed vocabularies
#               (`build/fx-hostgate --print-catalog` and
#               `build/fx-hostgate --print-host-tools` — which is also how a
#               reader checks this table against the vocabularies at rest)
#   decision    allow | deny   (no other value; the loader refuses anything else)
# THIS TABLE IS PINNED in policy/access/PINS.  Editing it is a RE-PIN — table
# and PINS in the same commit, so every edit to it is a visible release.  A
# stale or swapped table fails the pin check loudly at startup, naming both
# shas.
# fh_catalog_check's catalog, in table order (tools/fx-hostgate.c:2411-2423):
fx_query
fx_status
fx_activate
fx_rollback
fx_what
fx_why
fx_store_verify
fx_build
fx_outcome
fx_generation
fx_read
fx_write
fx_ls
# the HOST-TOOL registry, in table order (tools/fx-hostgate.c:2670-2673):
host_time
host_cat
